newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police seek lawmaker over MP's killing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police seek lawmaker over MP's killing.

text.p: Sri Lankan police on Wednesday were looking for an unnamed opposition lawmaker for questioning in connection with the killing of a member of parliament from the ruling coalition.

On Tuesday, gunmen killed People's Alliance parliamentarian Nalanda Ellawala during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals from the opposition United National Party (UNP). No arrests have been made.
A police statement on the killing was issued after Sri Lanka's two main political parties appealed for calm on the last day of nominations for local elections next month.
Ellawela's assailants also killed the guard of another ruling party legislator and wounded five people in the incident at Kuruwita, 80 km (50 miles) south of Colombo.
Police said a lawmaker from the UNP, his bodyguard and a former UNP mayor of Ratnapura, south of Colombo, were wanted for questioning over what police said was the assassination of Ellawala.
Police have not issued any arrest warrants.

"On the basis of the material available to the police so far, the following persons are wanted for questioning by police -- a UNP Member of Parliament of the Ratnapura District, his personal bodyguard and a former UNP mayor of Ratnapura Municipal Council," the statement said.
UNP general-secretary Gamini Athukorala said police should give the names.

"We don't know who the police are referring to. They must name the UNP member of parliament and they must name the former UNP mayor. Even I am a member of parliament from the Ratnapura district," Athukorala said.
Ratnapura police said none of the people being sought had appeared.
"They seem to have gone into hiding. We're looking for them," said an officer at the Ratnapura police station.
Police said a local night curfew was imposed again on Wednesday following sporadic rioting and arson. There were no arrests.
Witnesses said they saw mobs setting fire to shops of opposition UNP supporters but a senior police officer in the area denied reports of widespread violence.

Around the country, extra police were on duty in election offices as candidates and flag-waving supporters filed applications for the polls, the first electoral test for the ruling People's Alliance (PA) since it came to power in 1994.
The polls will be held in seven of the country's nine provinces. The government scrapped polls in the northern and eastern provinces because of guerrilla activity by Tamil separatists.

A total of 3,567 seats in assemblies in 12 cities, 31 towns and 195 villages will be contested along with the posts of mayor in Colombo and 11 other cities. The size of the assemblies ranges from nine seats in remote villages to 53 in Colombo.
Election day is tentatively set for March 27, with a firm date to be announced on Thursday, officials said.
